guardedCopilot.description: Guarded Copilot, Batch 1 (deterministic core): a read-only, lineage-citing chat-answer engine (js/agents/guarded-copilot.js) that composes the EXISTING AI Readiness Gate (js/gate/readiness-gate.js), the AI Touch Ledger (js/provenance/ai-touch-ledger.js -- also used to log Guarded Copilot's own queries), and the Story engine's grade vocabulary into deterministic Tier 1 answers for five supported questions (readiness/why-blocked, why-low-confidence, what-changed, who-touched-this, explain-grade). Tier 2 optionally reuses the exact on-device Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model already loaded for Story (js/narrative/ondevice-llm.js) to rephrase Tier 1's facts -- never a second model, never an external API -- and falls back to Tier 1's unmodified text with no WebGPU. Deliberately holds NO import of and NO call to the Agent Action Firewall's proposeAction/confirmAndApply, so it cannot initiate or complete a data mutation by construction; a structural red-team suite in test/guarded-copilot.test.mjs (34/0 passing) asserts this stays true. Batch 2 wired the read-only chat panel: a 'Copilot' tab (js/app-shell/main.js renderGuardedCopilotTab + #panel-copilot in index.html) that asks/displays only -- no write path -- and completes the real Tier 2 model call (refineWithOnDeviceModel now actually rephrases via the loaded on-device engine, still falling back to Tier 1 with no WebGPU/model). ENABLED LIVE (flag flipped true) after a live-preview One Confirm gate: the 'Copilot' tab is now in the nav bar for all users on web/desktop/PWA.

zkThresholdProof.description: Zero-Knowledge Threshold Proof (Batch 1): the FIRST genuine zero-knowledge proof primitive in DataGlow (js/provenance/zk-threshold-proof.js), distinct from every other js/provenance/ artifact (selective-disclosure-proof.js, verifiable-check-seal.js, portable-receipt.js, trust-beam.js), which are explicitly documented as NOT zero-knowledge (they commit to a value with a Merkle/SHA-256 tree and then reveal it in cleartext). This module is a non-interactive Schnorr Sigma protocol (Fiat-Shamir heuristic applied to a Pedersen commitment opening) over a deterministically-generated 512-bit safe-prime group (native BigInt modular exponentiation only -- zero third-party crypto library, zero WASM, zero new dependency, zero trusted-setup ceremony; group parameters are independently re-verifiable via selfCheckGroup()). Ships ONLY the 'equals zero' predicate this batch: proveZeroCriticalIssues() proves a dataset/query result has ZERO critical (fail-severity) validation flags WITHOUT revealing the actual count, which flags exist, or the underlying data -- a genuinely different guarantee than the Verifiable Check Seal's cleartext-disclosure model. Honestly scoped: this is NOT a general range proof (no 'x <= N' for arbitrary N -- that needs Bulletproofs-class engineering, a documented future batch, not implied to exist here), and the 512-bit group is sized for instant in-browser verification on any device including a phone, not maximum long-term security against a nation-state-level adversary (disclosed explicitly in the module's own ZK_PROOF_DISCLAIMER). If the statement is false (there ARE critical flags), proveZeroCriticalIssues() honestly REFUSES to fabricate a proof rather than lying. Wired as an opt-in 'Prove zero critical issues' button in the SQL tab's Local Analysis Contract flow (js/app-shell/main.js renderZkThresholdProofAffordance), alongside but independent of the existing Verifiable Check Seal button. Ships DARK (land-dark per the Build Nervous System convention): a human must click the button, nothing proves automatically, and with this flag off (its shipped default) no proof UI renders and the SQL tab behaves exactly as before this PR. 31/31 tests pass (test/zk-threshold-proof.test.mjs) covering completeness, soundness (tampered response/commitment/label/kind all correctly fail), and zero-knowledge (the secret blinding factor is never present in the serialized artifact).

queryVerificationSentinel.description: Query Sentinel (Batch 1): a per-query, deterministic static analyzer for the SQL tab distinct from the whole-dataset Local Analysis Contract (js/validation/analysis-contract.js). js/validation/query-sentinel.js checks four silent-bug classes on the query just run: FANOUT (a non-unique joined-side key before an aggregate can multiply rows and inflate a result), JOIN_KEY (a declared column-type mismatch across a JOIN ON condition), ADDITIVITY (a GROUP BY on a column that resolves to a non-unique joined-table column, so per-group totals won't sum to the ungrouped total), and SENSITIVE_COLUMN (delegates entirely to the existing classifySensitiveColumns/isSensitiveCategory predicate in js/agents/phi-prompt-guard.js -- no new pattern list). Pure logic, no DOM/DuckDB/network import, and degrades gracefully to a single info-severity hint rather than a false fail when a table's row count or a column's cardinality wasn't measured for the run -- the same graceful-degradation convention Local Analysis Contract uses. 22/22 tests pass (test/query-sentinel.test.mjs). Ships DARK: wired into the SQL tab's query-run path as its own independent branch with its own dismissible card; with this flag off (its shipped default) nothing imports the module and the existing SQL tab flow is byte-for-byte unchanged.

querySentinelAssist.description: Query Sentinel Assist (Batch 2 of 3): an opt-in, bounded on-device assist layered on top of Query Sentinel's (Batch 1, queryVerificationSentinel) already-computed FANOUT/JOIN_KEY/ADDITIVITY/SENSITIVE_COLUMN flags. Adds one button to the Query Sentinel card, 'Explain & suggest a fix'. Tier 1 (js/validation/query-sentinel-assist.js's assistDeterministic + buildFixSuggestion) is a zero-model, zero-cost, fully template-based per-rule-class fix-sketch lookup -- every possible output string is visible by reading the file, and it can never report a finding Batch 1 didn't already report. Tier 2 (assistWithOnDeviceModel) reuses the EXACT same on-device model js/narrative/ondevice-llm.js already loads for Story and Guarded Copilot (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct via WebLLM) -- no second model, no new WebGPU path -- purely to rephrase Tier 1's text into more natural language under a narrow system prompt that forbids inventing any new finding, severity, or fix idea; it falls back to the exact Tier 1 text whenever WebGPU/the model isn't available, matching Guarded Copilot's own Tier 2 fallback contract byte-for-byte. Architecturally incapable of writing/executing anything: no import of the DuckDB engine, no import of agent-action-firewall's confirmAndApply, no write/insert/delete/update/mutate/execute call anywhere in the file -- proven by a red-team structural test, not just by convention. 30/30 tests pass (test/query-sentinel-assist.test.mjs). Ships DARK and fully independent of queryVerificationSentinel's own flag: with this flag off (its shipped default) the assist button never renders and nothing imports query-sentinel-assist.js, so the SQL tab and the Batch 1 card are byte-for-byte unchanged.

querySentinelBridge.description: Query Sentinel Bridge (Batch 3 of 3, final): resolves `FROM py.<name>` / `FROM r.<name>` cross-runtime table references in the SQL tab against the Polyglot Workbench's Object Space registry (js/app-shell/object-space.js, Batch B) -- the working version of what that module's own header explicitly says it does NOT yet do ('no working FROM py.name yet'). js/validation/query-sentinel-bridge.js is a pure text-transform resolver: given the SQL string and the live listObjectSpace() array, it rewrites every exact `py:<name>` / `r:<name>` registry match to the real underlying DuckDB table (via each entry's provenance field) and returns an explicit resolved/unresolved list -- a near-miss or never-loaded name is left completely untouched (never a fuzzy/partial-match guess) and surfaced as an honest 'could not find X -- run that tab first' message, never a silent wrong-table substitution. HONESTLY SCOPED (confirmed by direct inspection of registerRuntimeObjects() and both language bridges): this only resolves references to datasets ALREADY LOADED and registered from a prior SQL/Python/R run -- it does NOT capture a brand-new, one-off variable a Python or R script computed inline that was never one of the app's loaded datasets; true arbitrary-variable capture is an explicit future batch, not implied to exist here. Wired into runSqlQuery() as a resolution pass immediately before the existing @metric expansion step -- when this flag is off (its shipped default) the resolver is never called and the SQL tab's query-run path is byte-for-byte unchanged; when on, a query with no py./r. reference at all also runs byte-for-byte unchanged (the resolver is a no-op pass-through). Architecturally incapable of writing/executing anything itself: no import of the DuckDB engine, no runQuery/createTableFromRows call, no write/insert/delete/update/mutate/execute call anywhere in the file -- the caller (main.js) still owns handing the rewritten SQL to the exact same engine.runQuery() path every other query already goes through. 31/31 tests pass (test/query-sentinel-bridge.test.mjs), including a red-team structural pass proving the no-DuckDB-import and exact-match-only guarantees. Ships DARK and fully independent of queryVerificationSentinel's and querySentinelAssist's own flags.

polyglotAutocomplete.description: Polyglot Workbench Batch D: schema-aware inline suggestions for the SQL, Python, and R editors (js/polyglot/polyglot-autocomplete.js). Suggestion pools are built from the live Object Space registry -- table names, column names (SQL: bare; Python: bracket notation; R: $ notation), and language-specific snippets (SQL keywords/functions, Python pandas fragments, R dplyr fragments). getSuggestions() returns scored, deduplicated suggestions; topSuggestion() returns the single best ghost-text suffix. Pure: no DOM, no DuckDB, no network. 40/40 tests.

polyglotErrorAdvisor.description: Polyglot Workbench Batch E: cross-language error messages with a grounded Suggested fix (js/polyglot/polyglot-error-advisor.js). Parses SQL/Python/R error strings into structured kind+detail+hint, then cross-references the Object Space registry to add a suggestedFix when the named identifier resolves to an object in a different language -- e.g. querying a Python-registered table in SQL suggests FROM py.name; referencing a SQL table in Python suggests dataglow.get_df(). Never fabricates a fix for an identifier not in the registry. renderAdvisedErrorHtml() produces an HTML snippet matching the existing formatSqlError/renderSqlErrorHtml shape. XSS-safe. 44/44 tests.

rigorEngineBadges.description: The Rigor Engine, Batch 2 of 4 (per NORTH_STAR.md's plan): honest per-group statistical confidence badges, plus the SQL→Visualize gap fix. js/rigor/statistical-rigor.js gains two new pure functions -- classifyGroupedConfidence(rows, groupCol, valueCol) runs the existing Batch-1 classifyConfidence() over EVERY distinct group in a GROUP-BY-shaped result (never a single verdict for a mixed result set), and summarizeGroupedConfidence() folds that into one conservative verdict for a compact badge by taking the WORST group's verdict, never an average. Two render surfaces share the exact same badge card (renderRigorBadgeCard in main.js): (1) the SQL tab auto-detects a categorical+numeric column pair in any query result and badges it via renderRigorConfidenceBadge(), and (2) the Visualize tab badges the currently-charted x/y pair the same way via renderVisualizeRigorBadge() whenever x is categorical, y is numeric, and the chart type isn't scatter (which has no grouping concept). Separately, this batch fixes a real gap found during investigation: populateVisualizeBuilder()/viz.renderChart() could ONLY ever read getActiveDataset() -- a SQL query's own result set had no path into a chart at all. renderSendToVisualizeAffordance() adds a 'Send to Visualize' button under every non-empty SQL result that registers the result as a real DuckDB table via the exact same engine.createTableFromRows/getTableSchema/addDataset sequence the existing Red Team v2 synthetic-dataset flow already uses, switches to Visualize, and pre-selects x/y from the same detection heuristic the badge uses. Every new code path is gated behind this flag: with it off (its shipped default) renderRigorConfidenceBadge/renderSendToVisualizeAffordance/renderVisualizeRigorBadge all return immediately on their first line, so the SQL tab, Visualize tab, and every existing badge/card render byte-for-byte unchanged. 56/56 tests pass (test/statistical-rigor.test.mjs, extended with 17 new cases for the two new functions plus a source-scan proving the module still names no DOM/network/DuckDB primitive).

temporalOrderChecks.description: Phase 2 -- Temporal Order Checker. Detects physically impossible event orderings within a single table (discharge before admit, lab result before order, payment before claim, death before birth, prior auth after service). Auto-detects date column pairs by name heuristic. Hard rule violations fail at any rate; soft rules use 0.1%/1% thresholds. Results in validationResults.relational.temporal.

flagConsistencyChecks.description: Phase 2 -- Flag Consistency Checker. Detects logical contradictions between binary flag columns. Built-in rules: readmit_30d=1 but readmit_90d=0, readmit_7d=1 but readmit_30d=0, inpatient=1 AND outpatient=1, emergency_admit=1 AND elective_admit=1, deceased=1 but discharge_disposition not expired (soft). Only runs rules whose requiredCols are all present. Supports custom extraRules.

joinCoverageChecks.description: Phase 2 -- Join Coverage Checker. Measures child-side join coverage rate (% of child rows that match a parent key). Thresholds: >=99% pass, 95-99% warn, 75-95% fail medium, <75% fail high. Complements FK orphan check. Stored in validationResults.relational.joinCoverage.

equityStratification.description: Phase 3 -- Equity Stratification Layer. Auto-detects race/ethnicity, sex/gender, zip/geography, payer class, age group, and disability/dual columns. Stratifies outcome metrics (readmission, denial, mortality, LOS, cost, ED utilization, quality score) by group using DuckDB GROUP BY queries. Scores disparities against CMS Disparities Impact Statement thresholds (rate ratio >= 1.5x or abs diff >= 5 pp = fail; 1.25x / 3 pp = warn). Builds a signed equity attestation block embedded in the Trust Certificate. Gated by this flag. Results in validationResults.equity. Fails open: any error produces idle status.

temporalDrift.description: Phase 4 -- Temporal Drift Layer. Computes freshness decay (trust score multiplier based on data age + rulepack stale/expiry thresholds), captures a statistical snapshot (row count, null rates, numeric means per column), and diffs against a prior snapshot when options.priorSnapshot is provided. Version-pins the active rulepack. Results in validationResults.temporal_drift. Fails open.

rulepacks.description: Phase 4 -- Versioned Rulepacks. All domain-specific thresholds (equity disparity, FK orphan rates, temporal order, join coverage, freshness decay) now come from a named rulepack rather than hardcoded constants. Built-in packs: healthcare (CMS/NCHS thresholds), general (domain-agnostic defaults). Custom packs can be registered at runtime via registerPack(). The active pack is version-pinned in the Trust Certificate.

joinBuilder.description: Phase 8 -- Multi-Table Visual Join Builder. Adds a "Join Builder" tab with an SVG drag-and-drop canvas. Users select tables from their loaded datasets, add them to the canvas as schema cards, draw join lines between columns (click-to-connect), change join type (INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL) by clicking an edge, and generate production-ready DuckDB SQL automatically. The Run query button pushes the generated SQL into the SQL tab and executes it. Ships enabled (not dark) because the feature is additive and has no risk to existing tabs.

nlSql.description: Phase 9 -- NL→SQL via Schema-Only + Metric Contracts. Adds an "Ask AI" tab where the user types a question in plain English and receives a DuckDB SQL SELECT statement. PRIVACY: only column names and types are sent to the LLM (never row data or patient records). Named metrics (readmission rate, denial rate, LOS, etc.) are resolved via Metric Contracts -- pinned SQL expressions that bypass LLM freestyle and produce reproducible, auditable SQL. Provider and API key configured per-session in the UI. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Perplexity. Ships enabled; the tab only shows when a provider and API key are configured.

dataVersionControl.description: Phase 10 -- Data Version Control. Adds a Versions tab where users can snapshot datasets (schema + stats only, no row data), diff any two snapshots side-by-side (schema changes + statistical drift detection with BREAKING/WARN/OK risk levels), and get advisory rollback info. Export/import snapshots as portable JSON. Snapshot fingerprinting prevents duplicate captures.

aiCouncil.description: Phase 11 -- Multi-Model AI Council. Adds a Council tab where the user asks one analytical question and gets answers from three LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini) called in parallel. The Council then synthesizes the results: CONSENSUS where all three agree, MAJORITY where two of three agree, and CONTESTED where all three differ, plus an overall agreement rating. Primary use case is data questions (for example: which metric best explains readmission risk, or what SQL computes denial rate) -- not general chat. PRIVACY: schema (column names + types) only is sent to each provider, the same guarantee as NL->SQL -- never row data or patient records. Provider and API keys are configured per-session in the UI and held in page memory only, never stored. Users can run the Council with 1, 2, or 3 providers enabled; synthesis only runs when at least 2 providers respond successfully.

serverOffload.description: Server offload (opt-in, user-configured endpoint required). When enabled, heavy queries CAN be delegated to a remote DuckDB instance ONLY when the user explicitly sets an endpoint URL. No data is ever sent without user-configured endpoint. DataGlow is local-first -- this flag makes the capability visible, not active. See js/app-shell/duckdb-config.js #8.

mcpInterface.description: AI Readiness Gate Batch 4 (MCP interface): exposes DataGlow's validation gate to any external AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) via the Model Context Protocol. Ships as a Node.js stdio MCP server (js/mcp/dataglow-mcp-server.mjs) that wraps the already-tested gate logic from Batch 1 (readiness-gate.js) and Batch 3 (agent-gate.js). Exposes: one tool (check_readiness -- returns agentConsumable verdict, score, failingLayers, reasons), two resource types per dataset (dataglow://schema/{name} and dataglow://validation/{name}), and two prompt templates (analyze_validated_dataset, fix_failing_layers). Reads a dataglow-gate-state.json file written by the browser app via js/mcp/gate-state-exporter.js when the user exports their gate result. Zero new validation logic -- the MCP layer is a thin typed adapter. Ships OFF: this flag gates the Settings tab Export Gate State button that triggers the file write; the MCP server process itself is always available to run manually via node js/mcp/dataglow-mcp-server.mjs regardless of flag state.

agentPassportBridge.description: Agent Passport Bridge: adds a new get_agent_passport MCP tool that composes FOUR already-live DataGlow signals into one JSON trust object for external MCP-calling agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client) -- the AI Readiness Gate verdict (readiness-gate.js, unchanged), Semantic Layer metric-contract status (ds.metricContractStatus as already exported, semantic-layer.js), AI Touch Ledger history/chain-verification (ai-touch-ledger.js's existing summarizeTouchLedger/verifyTouchLedger, now also carried through the gate-state export), and Verifiable Check Seal status (verifiable-check-seal.js's existing sealCheckResult output, the Proof Room tab's already-minted seal, also now carried through the export). Zero new checks, zero new crypto, zero new scoring -- every field is read verbatim or with a trivial pass-through mapping. Extends js/mcp/gate-state-exporter.js's buildGateStatePayload/serializeGateState with an optional, backward-compatible extras param (touchLedgerSummary, proofRoomSeal) and extends the Settings tab's Export Gate State button (main.js) to populate them from the browser's existing global AI Touch Ledger and Proof Room seal. Any missing signal is reported honestly (checked:false / available:false / sealed:false) rather than defaulted to a pass. Depends on the mcpInterface flag also being on (same Settings tab export gate). Ships OFF: with this flag off, get_agent_passport is still registered in ListToolsRequestSchema (matching check_readiness's own always-registered pattern) but is a net-new, additive tool -- no existing tool, resource, or prompt behavior changes. 81/81 tests in test/mcp-server.test.mjs (59 pre-existing + 22 new).

dataDiplomacyLoader.description: Data Diplomacy Batch 3: replaces the hardcoded two-claim demo scenario with a real data-loading UI (js/diplomacy/diplomacy-loader.js). Users pick any loaded dataset, choose entity-ID and value columns, enter the entity ID value to compare, and set source label + confidence + signer ID per party. The Reconcile button is enabled only when both claim forms are complete. The loader queries DuckDB to read the actual cell value for each party's row, then seals and reconciles using the same Batch-1 engine. The Batch-2 two-key approval UX renders below the forms after reconciliation completes. 25/25 tests. Paired with the top-level dataDiplomacy flag.

dataDiplomacyP2P.description: Data Diplomacy Batch 4: sealed-claim peer-to-peer exchange adapter (js/diplomacy/diplomacy-p2p-transport.js). DIPLOMACY_CLAIM_MESSAGE_KIND='diplomacy-claim'; buildClaimMessage()/isValidClaimMessage() are pure wire-format helpers; createDiplomacyP2PTransport({transport, selfId}) wraps any injected broadcast transport (typically a RoomBroadcastCoordinator) with sendClaim(claim)->Promise<boolean> and onReceiveClaim(fn)->unsubscribe(). NULL_DIPLOMACY_TRANSPORT is the no-op fallback when no Rooms session is active. Follows the exact dependency-injection discipline proven by federated-transport.js, room-signaling.js, and room-broadcast.js: unknown message kinds are silently ignored, handler errors never abort other handlers, destroy() tears down the subscription. Wired into renderDiplomacyTab in main.js when both dataDiplomacy and dataDiplomacyP2P flags are on: the loader form gains a 'Share claim with peer' button that calls sendClaim() with the locally sealed claim; onReceiveClaim() fills the other party's form from the incoming claim. Ships DARK: with the flag off the transport is never constructed and the Diplomacy tab is byte-for-byte unchanged. 30/30 tests in test/diplomacy-p2p-transport.test.mjs.

liveRoomsBroadcast.description: Live Rooms Batch 2: broadcast action items to peers via Rooms WebRTC transport. New pure adapter js/agents/live-rooms-broadcast.js adds a 'live-action-items' message kind on top of the existing Rooms data channel. LIVE_ACTION_ITEMS_MESSAGE_KIND='live-action-items'; buildActionItemsMessage({actionItems, meetingId, from})/isValidActionItemsMessage(msg) are pure wire-format helpers (build returns null for an empty items list; isValid requires the correct kind AND a non-null actionItems array); createLiveRoomsBroadcast({transport, selfId}) wraps any injected broadcast transport (the send(msg)/onReceive(fn) shape RoomBroadcastCoordinator uses) with broadcastActionItems(actionItems, meetingId)->Promise<boolean> (returns false on any failure, never throws) and onReceiveActionItems(fn)->unsubscribe() (handler errors never abort other handlers). NULL_LIVE_ROOMS_BROADCAST is the no-op fallback when no Rooms session is active. Follows the exact dependency-injection discipline proven by diplomacy-p2p-transport.js and room-broadcast.js. Wired into renderMeetingScribeTab in main.js when liveRoomsBroadcast is on and window.__dataglow_rooms_broadcast exists: the local grounded action-item list is broadcast to peers, and incoming remote items are merged into the local list and re-rendered so watchers see the list update live on their own device. Ships DARK: with the flag off the transport is never constructed and the Meeting tab is byte-for-byte unchanged. 35/35 tests in test/live-rooms-broadcast.test.mjs.

chartContextTimeline.description: Live Rooms Batch 3: real chart-context timeline wiring. New pure, Node-testable module js/agents/chart-context-timeline.js records which chart/query the analyst was viewing when each meeting line was spoken, so the Meeting Scribe feeds tagSegmentsWithContext a REAL timeline instead of an empty array (every tag was null before). buildChartContextEntry({chart, queryLabel, ts}) is a pure helper (chart must be a non-empty string, queryLabel defaults to null, ts defaults to Date.now(), returns null on bad input, never throws). createChartContextTimeline() returns recordChartView({chart, queryLabel, ts}) (silent no-op on bad input, never throws), getTimeline() (a frozen, safe copy -- mutating it never changes internal state), and clear(). Wired into main.js: when the flag is on, the SQL result render path calls recordChartView with the query text truncated to 60 chars, and renderMeetingScribeTab supplies chartContextTimeline.getTimeline() to mountMeetingScribe via a getContextTimeline option that the scribe passes to tagSegmentsWithContext. Ships DARK: with the flag off the singleton is never created, the scribe uses its default [] and every existing path is byte-for-byte unchanged. 26/26 tests in test/chart-context-timeline.test.mjs.

meetingSynthesis.description: Live Rooms Batch 4: on-device LLM synthesis panel for the captured meeting. New pure, Node-testable module js/agents/meeting-synthesis.js turns a grounded meeting note (the output of buildMeetingNote in js/agents/meeting-scribe-agent.js) into a focused prompt for the SAME on-device model the Story and Guarded Copilot tabs use, then packages the result. buildSynthesisPrompt(meetingNote) returns {systemPrompt, userPrompt} (both plain-language strings, always valid even for a null or empty note; the system prompt forbids inventing owners, dates, or numbers and asks for a four-part summary: pushback moments, data requests, action items, key grounding context). summarizeMeetingSynthesis(rawResponse, meetingNote) returns {summary, actionItemCount, pushbackCount, contextReferenceCount}, trimming the model text and drawing the counts from the note; never throws. isSynthesisAvailable() is a pure stub returning false, DI-wired in main.js to a WebGPU check (isOnDeviceSynthesisAvailable). Wired into the Meeting tab behind this flag via a separate host (#meeting-synthesis-body): a 'Synthesize with on-device model' button loads the model if needed (exact Story-tab progress + cancel pattern), runs buildSynthesisPrompt(currentMeetingNote) through the engine, and displays the summary plus grounding counts. Ships DARK: with the flag off the host stays empty and the Meeting tab is byte-for-byte unchanged. 26/26 tests in test/meeting-synthesis.test.mjs.

pivotTable.description: Pivot Table Batch 1: an Excel-style pivot builder answering the direct 'no pivot table UI exists' gap found this run. New pure, Node-testable module js/pivot/pivot-builder.js (zero DOM/browser globals) generates real DuckDB SQL from a {sourceTable, rows, columns, values} config -- buildGroupBySQL() for a Rows-only summary, buildPivotSQL() for a real DuckDB PIVOT ... ON ... USING ... GROUP BY cross-tab when a Columns well is populated, buildPivotQuery() as the single dispatch+validate entry point, plus classifyColumns()/validateConfig()/quoteIdent()/buildCardinalityCheckSQL() (a pre-flight distinct-combination count capped at MAX_PIVOT_CARDINALITY=200 to refuse silently generating a pivot with an unusable number of result columns). Deliberately reuses the existing DuckDB-WASM engine instead of a second, parallel JS aggregation implementation, so pivot numbers are provably the same numbers the SQL tab would produce for an equivalent hand-written query -- verified directly: 27/27 tests in test/pivot-builder.test.mjs run real generated SQL against a real in-test DuckDB table (not string-matching), including multi-measure Values, COUNT(col) NULL-handling, and quoted space-containing column names. The thin browser renderer js/runtimes-viz/pivot-ui.js owns the Rows/Columns/Values well UI -- a tap-to-add chip picker (never native HTML5 drag-and-drop, since DataGlow is mobile-primary and drag-and-drop is a poor touch fit), a Run Pivot button, and a result table reusing the same .result-table CSS the SQL tab uses. Wired into main.js behind this flag: a new 'pivot' tab id in TAB_META/state.tabOrder, gated in getVisibleTabIds() (the single source of truth per the code's own 'any new dark-flag tab only needs to be added HERE' comment), and a switchTab hook calling pivotUi.renderPivotTab(). Ships DARK: with the flag off the 'pivot' tab is never added to the bar, is never a dead click target, #panel-pivot stays empty, and every existing tab/module is byte-for-byte unchanged.

narrativeOverconfidenceGuard.description: Closes the gap named directly by the Stanford HAI 'delusional spirals' article (sycophancy/overconfidence in generated text): the Rigor Engine (all 4 batches complete) and story.js's buildStoryClaims() already grade every quantitative claim A-D and story.js's own generateLocalStory()/ondevice-llm.js's STORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT already INSTRUCT a model to hedge grade C/D claims -- but nothing previously verified the model's actual generated text obeyed that instruction. New pure, Node-testable module js/rigor/narrative-overconfidence-guard.js (zero DOM/network/model dependency) exports checkNarrativeOverconfidence(text, claims) -> {status: 'pass'|'warn'|'idle', findings}, which splits the narrative into sentences, locates the sentence(s) relevant to each claim (falling back to a whole-text scan for paraphrased claims, honestly reporting sentence:null when it can't localize), and for every grade C/D claim only (grade A/B claims are never flagged regardless of wording) checks two things: (1) overconfident language ('clearly', 'definitely', 'proves', 'always', 'never', '100% certain', etc.) attached to that weak claim, and (2) a total absence of hedge/caveat language anywhere in the narrative for that claim (the hedge check deliberately scans the WHOLE narrative, not just the claim-relevant sentence, since a real caveat sentence like story.js's own 'Treat this average cautiously -- it rests on limited or partly-missing data.' legitimately doesn't repeat the claim's number). describeOverconfidenceFinding() renders a plain-language line per finding. 29/29 tests in test/narrative-overconfidence-guard.test.mjs, including a source scan proving no DOM/network/DuckDB/model primitive is named. Wired into the Story tab in main.js: renderNarrativeOverconfidencePanel(storyText, queryResult) is called once, right after renderStoryClaims(), into a new #story-overconfidence-guard card sitting directly below the existing Narrative Consistency Check card -- reusing buildStoryClaims() so the guard checks the exact same claims/grades the visible per-claim badges already show, never a second independent scoring pass. Ships DARK: with the flag off, renderNarrativeOverconfidencePanel() returns on its first line before touching the DOM or re-deriving claims, #story-overconfidence-guard stays empty and display:none, and every existing Story tab render path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

portfolioNarrativeAssembler.description: Answers the analyst's own ask directly: can a full DataGlow session become one shareable write-up for a portfolio site, LinkedIn post, or resume attachment -- without re-deriving any numbers. New pure, Node-testable module js/portfolio/narrative-assembler.js (zero DOM/DuckDB/network dependency) exports buildCleaningSummary(issues, auditLog), buildNarrativeDocument({problemFramerMarkdown, storyDoc, issues, auditLog, recommendation, overconfidenceFindings, options}), renderNarrativeMarkdown(doc), and validateNarrativeDocument(doc). Stitches four things that already exist as separate modules: (1) Problem Framer's export markdown (js/problem-framing/problem-framer.js's buildExportMarkdown()), (2) the Story tab's narrative text, (3) a Clean tab issue/fix summary (built from js/cleaning/clean.js's scanForIssues() output plus the session's applied-fix audit log -- resolution is inferred from either a structured {issueId} entry or, matching DataGlow's real live audit-log shape, a quoted column name inside a freeform fix-description string), and (4) an analyst-authored closing recommendation, plus an optional Confidence Caveats section when the Narrative Overconfidence Guard has already flagged findings for the same story text. Fail-open throughout: never throws on missing/malformed input, always produces all 4 required section types so validateNarrativeDocument() always passes even with zero real input. 57/57 tests in test/portfolio-narrative-assembler.test.mjs, including live-app-shape audit-log strings and raw (no-status) narrative-overconfidence-guard.js finding objects. Wired into a new 'Portfolio' tab via js/portfolio/portfolio-ui.js (thin renderer, zero business logic): reads Problem Framer's live #framer-intake/[data-framer-q] inputs, state.lastStory, window.__dataglowLastCleanIssues + window.__dataglowAuditLog (both newly captured at their existing Clean-tab call sites), and window.__dataglowLastOverconfidence (newly captured alongside the existing Story tab's own overconfidence panel render) -- never re-running any of those four checks itself. Ships DARK: with the flag off, the 'portfolio' tab is filtered out of getVisibleTabIds() exactly like 'pivot', never added to the bar, never a dead click target, and #panel-portfolio stays empty; every existing tab's render path (including the two new window.__dataglow* capture lines, which are pure assignments with no conditional logic) is otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged.

sentinelGateway.description: Sentinel Local Agent Gateway -- typed, governed MCP-style interface to local DuckDB data with query budget enforcement and tamper-evident audit log

storageWatchdog.description: Cross-platform storage durability watchdog -- iOS ITP eviction warnings, Android Auto Backup risk notices, Tauri at-rest encryption guidance

offlineAICopilot.description: Sentinel Phase 3 -- Offline AI Copilot toggle. Routes NL queries through local WebGPU/WebLLM engine (Qwen2.5-Coder-3B) when on, falls back to WASM rule engine. Zero data egress on both paths.

securityAdvisor.description: Sentinel 3.5 -- SecurityAdvisor: Layer 1 regex threat model on SQL/Python/R before execution + proof chain integrity checks. All local, zero API calls. Surfaces findings in Sentinel governance panel.

teamHub.description: Team Hub (PR #554): DataGlow's multi-user collaboration foundation, added dark-safe and enabled by default since it is additive-only and touches no existing enabled:true path. Ships a Team button (data-testid=team-hub-btn) in the toolbar that opens a full-height slide-in panel (same style as the Sentinel governance panel). Mode A -- Artifact Exchange (works today, no setup): exportPackage() builds a Signed Analysis Package JSON bundle (dataset sample -- first 100 rows, SQL queries, ProofChain entries via window.ProofChain.getSteps(), chart configs, Sentinel audit log via window.SentinelGateway.getAuditLog()), signs it with the same sha256Hex/djb2-fallback pattern as proof-chain.js, and triggers a download; importPackage() reads a picked JSON file, validates its kind, and appends its ProofChain entries into the current session's real window.ProofChain. Works identically on web, Tauri desktop, and iOS/Android PWA since it is plain download/upload, no server. Mode B -- Quack Hub is a stub only (see quackHubSetup). Also ships the WebRTC P2P foundation named Sentinel Pillar 4 (see webrtcFoundation) and a Team Activity Feed reading the last 10 real ProofChain entries with a 'Share this proof chain' button that copies a base64url-encoded summary to the clipboard. Public API: window.DataGlowTeamHub = { getPeerId, connect, getStatus, exportPackage, importPackage }. No localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB -- the Peer ID persists via the existing window.OPFSEngine only. No external network calls -- WebRTC here never configures a STUN/TURN server (iceServers: []) and the Connect flow is a local signaling-stub only.

quackHubSetup.description: Quack Hub Setup (PR #554, part of Team Hub): the expandable 'Quack Hub Setup' section inside the Team Hub panel that explains DuckDB's forthcoming Quack multi-client protocol (GA expected Q4 2026) -- when available, a team can share a single DuckDB node and each analyst connects their DataGlow to it. Ships a duckdb://[host]:[port]/[database] connection-string input and a Test Connection button; clicking it is an intentional stub that shows a 'Quack Hub not yet GA -- coming Q4 2026' toast and never opens a real network connection. A 'Quack Hub: Coming Q4 2026' status badge with a BETA tag is always shown. No live DuckDB multi-client connection exists yet or is attempted -- that is future work gated on Quack actually reaching GA.

webrtcFoundation.description: WebRTC P2P Foundation (PR #554, Sentinel Pillar 4 groundwork, part of Team Hub): the Peer Connect subsection of the Team Hub panel. A random 8-char hex Peer ID is generated on first load and persisted in OPFS only (never localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB), shown at data-testid=team-hub-peer-id. A 'Connect to Peer' input + Connect button (data-testid=team-hub-connect-btn) drives a status indicator (data-testid=team-hub-status) that moves Disconnected -> Signaling... -> Disconnected in this batch, surfacing the toast 'Ready for WebRTC -- signaling channel stub wired. Full P2P sync ships in Sentinel Pillar 4 (Q3 2026).' A real RTCPeerConnection is instantiated with iceServers: [] (no STUN/TURN, matching the demo-mode LAN-only constraint) so the object's existence is verifiable by automated tests, but it is intentionally NOT wired to any live signaling server yet -- no P2P data channel is opened, no data is exchanged, and no external network call is made. Full peer-to-peer sync (real signaling server, data channel wiring, presence) is separate, later work explicitly named Sentinel Pillar 4.

mlInferencePanel.description: PR #553 -- ONNX-WASM Inference Panel. Drop a local .onnx model (stored in OPFS), inspect input/output tensor metadata, map dataset columns to input tensors, and run inference via onnxruntime-web (WebGPU when available, WASM fallback everywhere, WASM by default on iOS Safari). Predictions append as a new dataset column. Each run is signed into the ProofChain as a ml_inference record with model hash, input schema, and output distribution stats. Zero upload -- inference runs entirely on-device.

pipelineScheduler.description: PR #553 -- Service Worker Pipeline Scheduler. Define named SQL-transform pipelines (steps with name/sql/outputTable), schedule them (every 15 min, hourly, daily at midnight, or on file drop), and let the Service Worker wake the canvas to run them. Pipelines persist to OPFS. A CSS-only DAG visualizes step status, last run time, and row counts. Tauri gets a setInterval fallback since webview Service Worker scheduling varies. Every run appends a pipeline_run record to the ProofChain.

signedHtmlExport.description: PR #553 -- Signed HTML Dashboard Export. One-click export of a fully standalone HTML file: embedded datasets as CSV, chart configs (rendered via Chart.js from CDN inside the exported file, opened offline by the user), SQL query history, and the full ProofChain timeline with a prominent SHA-256 verification hash. Includes a Download Raw Data button and DataGlow Sentinel verification badge. iOS uses the share-sheet fallback when a direct download link does not trigger. Appends a dashboard_export record to the ProofChain.

modelRegistry.description: PR #553 -- ONNX Model Registry. Persistent, OPFS-backed catalog of registered models with automatic versioning (v2, v3, ... on re-add), tags, and schema metadata. Includes a Feast-compatible feature-group interface (named SQL queries producing feature vectors for model input) and point-in-time snapshot signing on every inference run (row count + column hashes + timestamp). A Model Audit Trail view lists all signed inference receipts per model. Appends model_registered, feature_group_defined, and inference_run records to the ProofChain.

vectorEngine.description: PR #555 -- VectorEngine core. A local vector similarity search engine using pure JS and typed arrays (Float32Array), API-compatible with LanceDB core operations so a real lancedb-wasm client can drop in with zero call-site changes once it ships (not production-ready as WASM as of July 2026). Embeddings use window.BrowserLLM tokenizer-derived vectors when the local model is loaded (WebGPU/WASM), falling back to a deterministic 64-dim character-hash embedding everywhere else -- always available on all four platforms with no model required. The in-memory index (Map of id/vector/metadata) persists to OPFS at opfs://vector-index/index.json with Float32Arrays serialized as base64. No localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB, no external network call for the index itself.

semanticQuerySearch.description: PR #555 -- Semantic Search UI in the NL query panel. Adds a collapsible Semantic Search section below the NL input bar with two search boxes: Find similar queries (searches the vector index of past NL queries) and Find columns by description (searches the vector index of dataset column names). Results render as clickable chips with similarity scores that populate the SQL editor. Pure JS, works identically on web, Tauri desktop, and iOS/Android PWA.

autoQueryIndexing.description: PR #555 -- Automatic Query and Column Indexing. Every NL query run through the NL panel is embedded and indexed (id query-<timestamp>, metadata sql/datasetName/ts). Every column name from every loaded dataset is embedded and indexed (id col-<datasetName>-<colName>, metadata dataset/dtype). Powers Find similar queries and Find columns by description. Also drives a Related queries section shown below SQL results with the 3 most similar past queries as clickable chips. Appends vector_indexed and vector_search records to the ProofChain.

lancedbCompat.description: PR #555 -- LanceDB Compatibility Shim. Exposes window.LanceDB with a LanceDB-style API (connect, openTable/createTable, table.add, table.search(vector).limit(k).toArray()) that wraps VectorEngine under the hood. When real lancedb-wasm becomes production-ready, this shim can be swapped for the genuine client with no changes to calling code.

provenanceFabric.description: PR #556 -- Provenance Fabric core. Upgrades the existing symbolic window.ProofChain ledger with a REAL cryptographic hash chain: every entry is SHA-256 hashed via crypto.subtle.digest (Web Crypto API, available on Chrome/Firefox/Safari desktop, the Tauri desktop webview, and iOS/Android PWA), with each hash computed over JSON.stringify({prevHash, ts, type, payload}) and linked to the previous entry's hash (genesis uses the hash of the empty string). window.ProvenanceFabric.append(type, payload) is async and returns {hash, seq, ts}; window.ProvenanceFabric.verify() re-hashes every entry and returns {ok, brokenAt, chainLength}. Wraps window.ProofChain.addStep so every existing call site (SQL history, Python/R/ML quality policies, find-replace, ONNX receipts, dashboard export, etc.) is mirrored into the cryptographic chain without any of those call sites being modified or removed. Falls back to a pure-JS FNV-1a hash (window.ProvenanceFabric.getCryptoMode() returns 'fnv-fallback') when crypto.subtle is unavailable, logging a one-time warning to the Sentinel panel. In-memory only for the session -- no localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB, no network calls.

regulatorAuditExport.description: PR #556 -- Regulator-Ready Audit Export. Adds window.ProvenanceFabric.exportAuditBundle(), which assembles the full cryptographic chain, a fresh verify() result, session metadata (platform detection for Tauri desktop / iOS PWA / Android PWA / web browser, DataGlow version, session start time), and summary stats (total operations, per-type breakdown, session duration) into one human-readable-header JSON file, downloaded client-side as dataglow-audit-<timestamp>.json. Adds an 'Export Audit Bundle' button to the existing Sentinel Governance panel (#dg-sentinel-panel), inserted via a MutationObserver next to the existing 'View Audit Log' / 'Done' controls since that panel's markup is built dynamically. Depends on provenanceFabric.

fabricIntegrityBadge.description: PR #556 -- Fabric Integrity status indicator. A small badge (green dot + 'Fabric intact', or red dot + 'Chain broken') mounted next to the existing Sentinel toolbar button, reusing the same toolbar-discovery selector ('.dg-toolbar, #dg-top-bar, .top-bar, header') as the existing Sentinel button injector so it appears consistently on web, Tauri desktop, and iOS/Android PWA layouts. Runs window.ProvenanceFabric.verify() once on app load and automatically again after every 10 new chain entries (via the dataglow:provenance-fabric-verified event), updating the badge color/text live. Depends on provenanceFabric.

roleProvenanceStamps.description: PR #556 -- Role-Specific Provenance Stamps. window.ProvenanceFabric.STAMPS ships pre-defined, labeled entry templates for the 19 data professional roles identified across DataGlow's cross-role research: named builders for Data Analyst (analysis_step: SQL query + result summary), Data Scientist (ml_experiment: model hash + metric snapshot), Data Engineer (pipeline_run: DAG step + row count), BI Developer (dashboard_publish: snapshot hash), Analytics Engineer (dbt_transform: model name + row delta), Healthcare Data Analyst (phi_access: column-mask count, zero PHI values ever recorded), Data Steward (governance_assertion: policy name + pass/fail), and ML Engineer (feature_store_snapshot: feature group + point-in-time hash); the remaining 11 roles (Data Architect, Data Governance Manager, Database Administrator, Business Intelligence Manager, Statistician, Research Analyst, Data Quality Analyst, MLOps Engineer, Data Product Manager, Marketing Analyst, Financial Data Analyst) share a generic role_action(role, action, detail) template so every role still gets an explicitly labeled, role-tagged provenance entry. window.ProvenanceFabric.stamp(name, ...args) is a convenience wrapper that builds and appends a named stamp in one call. Depends on provenanceFabric.

dataLens.description: DataLens column intelligence -- auto-profiles all columns on dataset load

phiShield.description: PHI Shield: one-button on-device privacy screen (Safe Harbor sample screen + PhiPromptGuard patterns + AI path fail-closed helper). Web+desktop+PWA. Screening aid only, not HIPAA certification.

excelHellRepair.description: Excel Hell Repair v1: on-device detection of the real header, junk title/blank/footer rows, multi-row header collapse, and type coercion into a reversible, refreshable Power Query-style recipe. Preview-first; Apply requires an explicit click; undo restores the pre-image. Web+desktop+PWA. Product face like PHI Shield with safe defaults.

pythonNotebooksLite.description: Python Notebooks-lite: multi-cell on-device Pyodide notebook (code + markdown cells, run cell/all, local .dgnb save/load) on top of existing Python runtime. Web+desktop+PWA. Not full Jupyter.

guidedUnpivot.description: Guided Unpivot: on-device wide-to-long reshape UI (keep cols + unpivot cols, preview, apply, glass-box DuckDB SQL). Web+desktop+PWA. Complements Pivot.

repairRecipeLibrary.description: Repair Recipe Library: save/list/reapply Excel Hell (and Guided Unpivot) prep recipes on-device via IndexedDB. Metadata only, no row upload. Web+desktop+PWA.

mobilePhiFirstRunCalm.description: Mobile-safe PHI chip + first-run calm strip: short on-device privacy labels, 44px touch targets, safe-area aware chip, quiet first-visit strip (no auto-dismiss). Web+desktop+PWA.

rNotebooksLite.description: R notebooks-lite any-industry: multi-cell on-device WebR notebook (code+markdown), DuckDB table bridge, ggplot2 best-effort, .dgrnb save/load. Stats/finance/bio/ops/healthcare-ready, not pharma-only. Web+desktop+PWA.

notebookToApp.description: Notebook to App. Adds a Save as app button to the Python and R notebook toolbars that turns a notebook which already ran on this device into ONE self-contained HTML file: the cells, the captured text output and the captured plots, in a calm read-only surface that opens by double click with no server, no install and no internet. Ships ON: the button mounts on both notebook toolbars, and nothing is written until the human presses Save in a confirm sheet that lists in plain language exactly what goes in the file. PHI Shield scans the notebook text first and a hit preselects leaving the results out. Air-Gap Mode does not refuse it, since the file is built here and calls nothing, and the builder refuses to emit a file that references anything off the device. No dataset rows, no keys, no cookies, no tracking. Web+desktop+PWA. A snapshot of a run, not a live notebook.
notebookToApp.flagOffBehavior: No Save as app button on either notebook toolbar; the notebooks and their .dgrnb save/load are untouched.

trustLedger.description: Trust Ledger. One calm append-only list of this session's trust events, oldest first: a validation score, a metric definition version, an export that was written, a gate verdict. Adds a Trust button next to Air-Gap and Shield Packs that opens a side panel where every row is a plain sentence a human can read, plus the first 16 characters of its hash. Rows are chained with SHA-256 exactly the way js/provenance/provenance.js and the AI Touch Ledger already do (same genesis anchor, same canonical-JSON discipline, same digest), so this composes the existing provenance rather than inventing a second crypto stack; a Verify the chain button re-walks it and says plainly if a row was edited, reordered or removed. Malformed input is appended as a visibly refused row rather than dropped, so the ledger cannot be quietly incomplete. Ships ON: the button mounts on every load. Session-scoped and in memory only, so closing the tab ends it: nothing is written to localStorage, cookies or IndexedDB and no network call is made. The Save as text, Markdown and JSON buttons are the only way a row leaves, and they write one file to this device. It never edits a row, and it records nothing on its own beyond the events the app already fires. Web+desktop+PWA. A record of what this session did, not an audit certification.
trustLedger.flagOffBehavior: No Trust button and no panel, and the event listeners are not installed, so nothing is recorded automatically. window.DataGlowTrustLedger is still published so an explicit caller can append, but open() refuses.

publishSafe.description: Publish-Safe. The single gate that combines what DataGlow already knows before a file is written or shared, so no export path has to remember to ask all four checks itself: PHI Shield on the exact text that would travel, the readiness gate on the dataset behind it, Metric Contracts on whether the definitions are still the agreed ones, and Air-Gap Mode on whether the human asked for nothing to cross the network. It returns one plain-language verdict of clear, caution or blocked plus a suggested safer default, and the caller must still show it and wait. Sensitive values plus a destination off this device is the one hard refusal, because a file that has left cannot be unshared. Sensitive values staying on this device is a caution with leaving the results out preselected, not a refusal, because the human owns the disk. Failing readiness or a drifted metric definition is a caution and never a block, since those are quality signals and not privacy ones. A check that could not run is never reported as a pass. Wired into the Save as app confirm sheet, where it shows the verdict above the choice and records the outcome in the Trust Ledger. Pure and side-effect free: it gathers no evidence of its own, mutates nothing, writes nothing and decides nothing for the human. Web+desktop+PWA. A gate over the checks it was given, not a guarantee about what it was never shown.
publishSafe.flagOffBehavior: No surface reads this as a flag today: the engine is consulted only when window.DataGlowPublishSafeEngine is present, and the Save as app sheet behaves exactly as it did before Publish-Safe existed when it is absent. Recorded here so the capability is named and the promote-or-delete clock starts.

airGapMode.description: Air-Gap Mode. When ON, hard-blocks outbound network for AI/MCP/serverOffload paths (plus CDN runtime downloads, telemetry, Rooms and federated learning). Local DuckDB/SQL/Python/R/charts keep working. Calm banner. Fail-closed: anything not on the on-device allowlist is blocked while active. Session-scoped and in-memory, nothing written to storage. Ships ON (promoted 2026-07-25, feat/enable-air-gap-mode-on): the toggle, panel and banner mount on every load, so the switch is there without a console opt-in. Engaging the block stays the user's own session-scoped choice, and the same toggle turns it back off for the session; nothing is persisted either way. Set window.DATAGLOW_AIR_GAP = false before boot, or serve a flags provider that reports airGapMode disabled, to keep the surface off entirely. Complements the deployment-level Enterprise No-Egress policy (js/build/enterprise-policy.js), which an administrator sets; this one is the user's own switch for the session. Web+desktop+PWA. Blocks DataGlow's own outbound paths, not a firewall.

shieldPacks.description: Shield Packs: one calm on-device surface listing domain privacy packs. Pack 0 is the existing PHI Shield, reused not reimplemented (the phiShield flag stays independent and keeps working on its own). Adds three packs: Finance PII (SSN/EIN/account/card/IBAN shapes, detect and flag only, never uploads), Privilege labels (attorney-client style column tagging plus an export caution, not legal advice), and Justice sensitive (CJIS-style shell with a high-sensitivity banner that fails closed by blocking AI and export paths while active). Session-scoped activation, in-memory only, no storage. Web+desktop+PWA. Screening aid only, not a compliance certification.

explain.description: Explain (Bundle 5, A13): the plain-language door into evidence DataGlow already has. js/explain/explain-engine.js is the PURE, Node-testable composer -- explainResult() gathers what seven named sources reported (Query Sentinel, the readiness gate, result shape, PHI Shield, Air-Gap Mode, Publish-Safe and the Trust Ledger), turns each into one calm sentence, and returns an explanation carrying its own confidence: well-evidenced when every source answered, partly-evidenced when some did not, unevidenced when a clear majority could not. It never invents certainty: a source that could not run is reported by name as an unknown rather than omitted or passed, because a missing check silently reading as clean is the one failure that would make the whole panel untrustworthy. js/explain/data-glow-explain-canvas.js is the canvas surface: a panel beside Trust and Air-Gap that reads the same gates GlassBox reads, so the two cannot disagree, and offers the explanation as copyable plain text. Enabled because the surface is complete: it mounts, composes from real published state, and degrades to naming what it could not see.
explain.flagOffBehavior: No Explain button and no panel mount. window.DataGlowExplain is still published, so a caller can compose an explanation programmatically; nothing in the app depends on the panel existing.

glassBox.description: GlassBox (Bundle 5, A15): the show-the-math block under a finding. js/glassbox/glass-box.js is the PURE, Node-testable model -- buildGlassBox() puts the finding on top and the proof underneath, returning the actual code that ran, which engine ran it, and a fixed-order badge row read only from gates that genuinely reported. A gate that is absent produces no chip at all rather than a passing one, and the model says out loud that an absence of evidence is not a clean result. Source longer than 60 lines is truncated with the real line count kept, so the panel is never quietly partial. js/glassbox/data-glow-glass-box-canvas.js mounts the block on the three real result surfaces (the SQL view result, the SQL tab result and the Python result), reading the paired editor at the moment the block opens so the code shown is the text a person can see above it. Nothing is reconstructed and nothing is cached: a guessed query would look checkable and be wrong. Enabled because the surface is complete on all three hosts.
glassBox.flagOffBehavior: No blocks mount under any result. window.DataGlowGlassBox is still published so a model can be built without a block existing; result rendering is untouched either way.

priorPeriodCompare.description: Compare to prior period (Bundle 6, A18): month over month, week over week, day over day, per entity if the table has one. js/transforms/prior-period.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. Its one load-bearing decision is what "prior" means: not LAG(value) OVER (ORDER BY period), which returns the previous ROW and therefore compares March against January whenever February is missing, but the previous CALENDAR period, looked up by a stepped-back period key. When that period is absent the prior value is null, the delta is null, and the result says so in its notes rather than presenting a gap as a comparison. The generated SQL is a LEFT JOIN on the stepped-back period key rather than a bare LAG, so the proof matches the rows. Percent change is null when the prior is zero, because printing Infinity next to real numbers invites someone to act on it. Enabled because the tab mounts in the Time and joins panel with confirm before apply.
priorPeriodCompare.flagOffBehavior: The Prior period tab is not rendered in the Time and joins group of the Transforms panel. If every tab in that group is off the group itself is not offered, and if all ten transform flags are off the panel and its button do not mount at all. window.DataGlowPriorPeriod is still published so the engine can be called programmatically.

dateRangeJoin.description: Join on date range (Bundle 6, A19): match each event to the reference row whose span contains its date. js/transforms/date-range-join.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. A range join has no intuition attached the way a key join does, so two reference ranges overlapping by one day silently double every event on that day and every total taken afterwards. previewDateRangeJoin() therefore counts matched, unmatched, the worst fanout and the number of multi-match rows WITHOUT building rows, and the panel shows that before anything is applied. Two boundary rules are stated rather than guessed: a blank end date means still in force (configurable), and bounds are inclusive on both sides by default (configurable). Both appear in the generated non-equi SQL as an explicit OR end IS NULL and a <= rather than a <. An end date that is present but unreadable is never read as open. Enabled because the tab mounts with preview and confirm before apply.
dateRangeJoin.flagOffBehavior: The Date range tab is not rendered in the Time and joins group. window.DataGlowDateRangeJoin is still published for programmatic use.

firstLastEvent.description: First or last event per entity (Bundle 6, A20): one row per group, chosen by an order column, or every row kept with its rank. js/transforms/first-last-event.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. The problem it solves is ties, not ordering: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY entity ORDER BY ts DESC) may return either of two rows sharing a timestamp, and may return a different one next run, which is a report that changes when nothing changed. The tie-break here is total and stated: after the order column, rows are compared by every remaining column in table order, identically in the JS engine and in the generated DuckDB QUALIFY / ROW_NUMBER SQL, where it appears in the ORDER BY rather than in prose. When ties actually occurred the notes say how many and admit the choice was repeatable but arbitrary. Rows with no readable order value are excluded and counted, never defaulted to the epoch. Enabled because the tab mounts with confirm before apply.
firstLastEvent.flagOffBehavior: The First / last tab is not rendered in the Time and joins group. window.DataGlowFirstLastEvent is still published for programmatic use.

asOfLookup.description: As-of lookup (Bundle 6, A24): for each fact row, the reference row that was in force on that date. js/transforms/as-of-lookup.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. It prevents the most expensive error in this bundle: joining a sale to a price table on product id alone gives today's price, which multiplied by last year's units is revenue that never happened, in a number that looks completely ordinary. Three refusals are deliberate. A fact dated before every reference row gets NULL, never the oldest row on record, because the oldest value is not the value that was true then. Two reference rows sharing one effective date are a real ambiguity, so the later one in table order is used AND the count is reported. A fact whose date cannot be read is blanked and counted rather than looked up as of today. The glass-box SQL is DuckDB's ASOF LEFT JOIN with the equivalent ROW_NUMBER form underneath for engines that lack it. Brought columns always carry an _asof suffix, so a point-in-time value cannot be mistaken for a current one two steps later. Enabled because the tab mounts with confirm before apply.
asOfLookup.flagOffBehavior: The As-of tab is not rendered in the Time and joins group. window.DataGlowAsOfLookup is still published for programmatic use.

expandHierarchy.description: Expand a hierarchy (Bundle 7, A16): a parent/child or path column becomes one row per node with its depth, its parent, the root it sits under, its full path and whether it is a leaf. js/transforms/expand-hierarchy.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. The load-bearing decision is what happens to a broken tree, because real org charts and account trees are broken: a node whose parent id is not in the table, and a node that is its own ancestor. Neither is dropped and neither is followed forever. Unreachable nodes are emitted with a null depth and an in_cycle marker, and the walk is bounded at 256 levels, so a self-referencing row produces a report instead of a hung tab. The glass-box SQL is a WITH RECURSIVE CTE seeded on the rows with no findable parent, carrying the visited list so the cycle guard in the SQL is the same guard the engine used. Enabled because the tab mounts in the Shape and clean group with confirm before apply.
expandHierarchy.flagOffBehavior: The Hierarchy tab is not rendered in the Shape and clean group of the Transforms panel. window.DataGlowExpandHierarchy is still published so the engine can be called programmatically.

nestedToRows.description: Nested lists into rows (Bundle 7, A17): a column holding JSON arrays or separated text becomes one row per element. js/transforms/nested-to-rows.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. Two things make it more than a split. First, the row count: previewNestedToRows() counts the output WITHOUT building it, so the panel can say "1,204 rows would become 38,911" and warn above the run button rather than after a browser tab has already tried to hold the result. Second, empty lists: a plain UNNEST drops those rows silently, and a row disappearing from a count is harder to notice than a blank cell, so they are kept by default with a blank element and the count is reported. A cell that looks like JSON and does not parse is reported as unreadable rather than split on a comma and passed off as a list. Complementary to js/ingestion/json-flattener.js, which widens an object into columns; this lengthens a list into rows. Enabled because the tab mounts with a row-count preview and confirm before apply.
nestedToRows.flagOffBehavior: The Nested lists tab is not rendered in the Shape and clean group. window.DataGlowNestedToRows is still published for programmatic use.

fillMissingFlagged.description: Fill blanks and flag them (Bundle 7, A25): forward fill from the last value above, or a constant you choose. js/transforms/fill-missing.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. Every filled column gets a companion _was_filled boolean column, and that is not configurable: an invented value that reads like a measured one is the entire risk of this transform, and a fill with no flag is indistinguishable downstream from data that was always there. Only two modes ship, because a group mean needs its own honest account of what it assumes and js/cleaning/imputation.js already offers the statistical modes; the runtime notes say plainly that the wizard does not add a flag column, so a person choosing between them knows the difference. Forward fill needs an order column and sorts rows with no readable order value last, where they are never filled, because carrying a value into a row whose position is unknown is guessing twice. Enabled because the tab mounts with confirm before apply.
fillMissingFlagged.flagOffBehavior: The Fill blanks tab is not rendered in the Shape and clean group. window.DataGlowFillMissing is still published for programmatic use.

expandDailyRows.description: Date range into daily rows (Bundle 7, A26): a start and end date per row become one row per calendar day, which is the occupancy and bed-days shape. js/transforms/expand-date-range.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. This is the highest multiplier in the bundle, so the count comes first: previewExpandDateRange() counts the output days without building any, warns at 100,000 rows and at 20,000 on a narrow screen, and refuses outright above 2,000,000 BEFORE anything is built, so a refusal never leaves a half-expanded table behind. There is deliberately no "up to today" option: an open-ended range is skipped unless a person states an as-at date, and that date is written into both the notes and the generated SQL as a literal, because a table that silently used current_date would give a different answer every time it was built. An end date that is present but unreadable is not treated as open. The end day counts by default and that convention is stated in the notes, since both conventions are in use. Glass-box SQL is a CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series. Enabled because the tab mounts with a row-count preview and confirm before apply.
expandDailyRows.flagOffBehavior: The Daily rows tab is not rendered in the Shape and clean group. window.DataGlowExpandDateRange is still published for programmatic use.

visualBinEditor.description: Group a number into bands (Bundle 7, A27): equal-width bands by default, or edges you type. js/transforms/bin-editor.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine, and the histogram comes from the same binCounts() the apply uses rather than from a separate pass, so the bars a person read and the bands they applied cannot disagree. Equal-width binning is quietly wrong on skewed data, where one large value stretches the range and everything else lands in the first band, so the engine warns when a single band holds 90 percent or more of the rows and points at custom edges. Bands are half-open, stated in the labels, the notes and the generated CASE ladder, with only the top band including its own upper edge. A value outside the edges gets a blank band rather than being pushed into the nearest one, because the values worth looking at are exactly the ones that fell outside. Separate from the chart histogram in js/chart/chart-engine.js, which draws a picture; this adds a column. Enabled because the tab mounts with a live histogram and confirm before apply.
visualBinEditor.flagOffBehavior: The Bands tab is not rendered in the Shape and clean group. window.DataGlowBinEditor is still published for programmatic use.

keepMostRecent.description: Keep the most recent per group (Bundle 7, A29): entity keys plus an order column leave one row per group. js/transforms/keep-most-recent.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. Unlike A20, which answers a question, this deletes rows that were in the table a moment ago, so the number it leads with is not "rows removed" but "rows removed that disagreed": dropping an exact copy loses nothing, while dropping a row that shared the key and held a different address or amount throws away a fact. The result counts those groups separately and names the columns where the discarded rows disagreed with the row kept, which is what says whether this was a de-duplication or a choice. Ties are broken by every remaining column in table order, identically in the engine and in the generated ROW_NUMBER SQL, and the notes admit that repeatable is not the same as correct. A row whose order value cannot be read is kept by default, because deleting a row on the strength of a mistyped date is a loss nobody asked for. It shares sortableOrderValue and compareValues with A20 through js/transforms/transform-core.js rather than copying them, so the two cannot come to disagree about what latest means. Enabled because the tab mounts with confirm before apply.
keepMostRecent.flagOffBehavior: The Keep recent tab is not rendered in the Shape and clean group. window.DataGlowKeepMostRecent is still published for programmatic use.

consecutiveRun.description: Consecutive runs (Bundle 8, A21): gaps-and-islands over an entity plus a date column, giving one row per unbroken streak of active days. js/transforms/consecutive-run.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. The arithmetic it refuses to hide is that a streak is a run of DAYS and not a run of ROWS: two rows on the same date are one active day, so a duplicated export lengthens nothing, and the collapsed rows are counted and reported rather than silently absorbed. The generated SQL leads with SELECT DISTINCT over the entity and the cast date for exactly that reason, then subtracts a ROW_NUMBER from the date to form the island key. A run that reaches the end of the data has not ended, it has run out of data, so an optional as-of date adds a still_running column and the notes say how many runs are open; without an as-of date no such claim is made at all. Rows whose date cannot be read are dropped and counted, never treated as a gap. Enabled because the Runs tab mounts in the Advanced group with confirm before apply.
consecutiveRun.flagOffBehavior: The Runs tab is not rendered in the Advanced group. window.DataGlowConsecutiveRun is still published for programmatic use.

movingAverageCross.description: Moving average with optional crossover (Bundle 8, A22): a trailing average over an ordered column, optionally a second window, optionally a column marking where the two cross. js/transforms/moving-average.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. The silent wrongness it exists to stop is a 7 row average of 2 rows presented as a 7 row average, so warm-up rows are blank by default and every row carries rows_in_window stating how many values actually went into it; the partial mode is offered but says in the notes that early rows are not comparable to later ones. A crossover requires both averages on the current row AND on the row before it, so the first row where both exist is never reported as a crossing, which is the classic false signal at the start of a series. Calendar gaps inside the window are detected and stated, because a row-count window over a series with missing days covers more calendar than its label claims. Grouping restarts the window per series so no average mixes two entities. Enabled because the Moving avg tab mounts in the Advanced group with confirm before apply.
movingAverageCross.flagOffBehavior: The Moving avg tab is not rendered in the Advanced group. window.DataGlowMovingAverage is still published for programmatic use.

multiValueMembership.description: Multi-value field counts (Bundle 8, A23): a column holding "Cardiology; Endocrinology" or a JSON array is split and counted per category rather than per combination. js/transforms/multi-value-counts.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. Splitting makes the counts sum to more than the number of records, which is what multi-membership means and is not an error; the error is a percentage denominator that implies exclusivity, so every count carries TWO labelled percentages: pct_of_records (share of records, sums above 100 whenever a record has several values) and pct_of_mentions (share of mentions, sums to 100). Both are shown because either alone gets misread as the other, and the notes state the actual sum out loud whenever it exceeds 100. A record is counted once per category and not once per mention, so "asthma, asthma" is one record with asthma; the duplicate mentions are counted separately because a column full of them is usually a concatenation bug. Records with no value stay in the denominator, since removing them inflates every percentage. Enabled because the Multi-value tab mounts in the Advanced group with confirm before apply.
multiValueMembership.flagOffBehavior: The Multi-value tab is not rendered in the Advanced group. window.DataGlowMultiValueCounts is still published for programmatic use.

frequentCombinations.description: Frequent combinations (Bundle 8, A28): pair frequency across several category columns or within one multi-value column, with support counts. js/transforms/frequent-combinations.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. The arithmetic it refuses to hide is that a big pair count is usually just two common values meeting by arithmetic rather than by association, so every pair ships count_a, count_b and a lift computed as visible division against what independence would predict; ranking by raw support alone ranks popularity. Each unordered pair appears once, enforced by an item_a < item_b inequality in both the engine and the generated SQL, because emitting the mirror image doubles every count. Pairs resting on very few records are flagged as a hint rather than a measurement, since a lift of 7 on one record is noise. Records are capped for pair explosion and any truncation is counted and stated. Enabled because the Combinations tab mounts in the Advanced group with confirm before apply.
frequentCombinations.flagOffBehavior: The Combinations tab is not rendered in the Advanced group. window.DataGlowFrequentCombinations is still published for programmatic use.

windowRecurrence.description: Within-window recurrence (Bundle 8, A30): index event to return event pairs plus a rate, for questions of the "another one within 30 days" shape. js/transforms/window-recurrence.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. The load-bearing arithmetic is censoring: an event in the last N days of the data has not had N days to recur, so counting it as no return drags the rate down for calendar reasons. Two rates are therefore reported, one over events with a full window available and one over every event, alongside the censored count and the observation end, and the panel shows both stacked above the pairs table so the answer is not the thing that scrolled off a tablet. Each index event pairs with only the NEXT event, never with every later one, so three events give two pairs rather than three and the count is not quadratically inflated. The smallest gap defaults to one day, so two events on the same date read as one event entered twice rather than as an instant return. Enabled because the Recurrence tab mounts in the Advanced group with confirm before apply.
windowRecurrence.flagOffBehavior: The Recurrence tab is not rendered in the Advanced group. window.DataGlowWindowRecurrence is still published for programmatic use.

valueStandardizer.description: Value standardizer (Bundle 8): distinct values of a category column, proposed merge groups, a human-confirmed map, and a glass-box UPDATE. js/transforms/value-standardizer.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. Nothing is applied without confirmation and the proposal is not the map: proposeMergeGroups returns groups and no map at all, the panel lets any group be switched off, and validation refuses any config whose confirmed flag is not literally true. Merges are deterministic by default (case, whitespace, punctuation) because those are reversible facts about the text; similarity scoring is a guess, so it only runs when a clusterer is injected and its groups are labelled as guesses. Canonical choice prefers a tidy, deliberately capitalised spelling over the merely most frequent one, so a stray leading space is not propagated into every row. A chained recode (a to b while b to c) is refused outright, because the answer would depend on which replacement ran first. An audit column captures the original value BEFORE the update, in that order in the generated SQL, since afterwards the old spelling exists nowhere. Enabled because the Standardise tab mounts in the Shape and clean group with confirm before apply.
valueStandardizer.flagOffBehavior: The Standardise tab is not rendered in the Shape and clean group. window.DataGlowValueStandardizer is still published for programmatic use.

proofBoard.description: Proof Board (Bundle 9): several numbers on one surface, each with the query that produced it in the same tile. js/proofboard/proof-board.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine and js/proofboard/session-tiles.js computes the tiles from the rows actually loaded. Nothing on the board is seeded: with no dataset the grid shows its empty state and one call to action, because a demo number on a surface whose promise is that every number shows its work would be a fabricated proof. The gate badge has four values and not two, so an absence of checks reads as Not checked and can never be promoted to a pass by nothing having gone wrong; the badge is read off a real gate result when one is supplied and the tile's own label is overridden, with the disagreement recorded, when the two differ. A malformed tile is kept and marked incomplete rather than dropped, since a missing tile is much harder to notice than one that says what is wrong with it. Verify board checks only what the board holds and names what it cannot check, and it never re-runs a query. Export Glowbook writes one self-contained HTML file with no script and no network, and only after a human confirms. Stamp receipt appends to the Trust Ledger, also after a confirm, and writes no crypto of its own. Enabled because the Proof button and panel mount beside the Trust Ledger.
proofBoard.flagOffBehavior: Neither the Proof button nor the panel is created, so the surface is absent from the page and the coach strip cannot appear. window.DataGlowProofBoard, window.DataGlowGlowbook and window.DataGlowProofBoardTiles are still published for programmatic use, and window.DataGlowProofBoardUI reports mounted false with open() still available.

proofBoardCoach.description: Proof Board coach strip (Bundle 9): five short steps that point at real controls in the Proof Board panel. js/proofboard/coach-moments.js is PURE data plus small pure helpers, not a tour framework: nothing is dimmed, nothing is blocked and the panel stays fully usable with the strip open.
