There is no video and no asset, so the page still reaches no network. A step whose target element is missing is skipped rather than pointed at nothing. Once dismissed it stays dismissed, because a tip that returns on every open stops being a tip and the person who most needs to get work done is the one who has opened the panel most often. Separate from the whole-app journey in analyst-journey.js, whose four moments are hard-coded and which publishes no way to register more. Enabled because the strip mounts on first open of the Proof Board.
proofBoardCoach.flagOffBehavior: The strip never opens and no dismissal flag is written. The Proof Board panel itself is unaffected, and window.DataGlowProofBoardCoach is still published so the steps can be read programmatically.

aiProveGate.description: Prove gate (Bundle 10): before any assembled or narrated claim is shown, every number in it is bound to a Proof Board tile or an engine result, and the ones that do not bind are named. js/ai/prove-gate.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. A number is allowed through on an exact match or on a correct rounding to the precision the author actually wrote, and on nothing else, so a claim cannot drift a value and call it a summary. A tile carrying the blocked badge refuses outright, because quoting a number a check has already objected to would publish a known problem; a tile carrying the unknown badge binds but raises a caution, since an absence of checks is not a pass. ISO dates, clock times and version strings are masked before extraction so the gate does not refuse the method line it ships with. Enabled because the Proof to Post draft is validated through it on every render.
aiProveGate.flagOffBehavior: The prove gate is not consulted, so the Proof to Post surface reports its draft as unvalidated and the Copy draft button stays disabled. window.DataGlowProveGate is still published for programmatic use and still refuses unbound numbers when called directly.

proofToPost.description: Proof to Post (Bundle 10): the last step of the verified analyst loop, where a proved number becomes a post without being retyped. js/proofpost/proof-to-post.js is the PURE, Node-testable engine. The draft is assembled from Proof Board tiles and from nothing else, so every number in it came out of an engine by construction, and it is then run back through the prove gate anyway because assembly can go wrong and a post cannot be recalled. NEVER_AUTO_POST is a constant and not a setting: there is no connected account, no posting API and no outbound request, and the last action is always a human pasting text they have read. The transparency line is computed from the badges actually present rather than written as a fixed string, so the post cannot claim its numbers were engine-checked in exactly the case where some were not. proofHarness.description: Proof Harness v0 (VERDICT), the first slice of the doctrine in MASTER_PROMPT_DataGlow_VERDICT_Proof_Harness_July_2026.md: 'AI proposes. Engines prove. The human confirms.' js/proof-harness/proposal.js is the ONLY door into execution -- createTypedProposal({statement, engine, expected, tables, author, claimText}) validates the shape and returns a frozen proposal carrying a sha256 digest over its executable content (statement/engine/expected/tables; author is excluded from the digest on purpose, since the same statement proposed by AI or by a human is still the same thing to prove). There is no sibling call that lets a raw model string reach an executor. js/proof-harness/verdict.js's decideVerdict() returns exactly one of GREEN (proven), RED (refuted), or GRAY (not provable, blocker named) -- v0 does not implement AMBER staleness, that is v1 -- and never attaches a confidence percentage to the verdict itself. js/proof-harness/score-claim.js restates drill-floor.js's scoreDrillAnswer/scalarMatches epsilon-and-trim comparison discipline (rowCount plus named scalars) rather than inventing a new one. js/proof-harness/receipt.js is an append-only, SHA-256 hash-chained ledger of receipts shaped like the MASTER PROMPT's in-toto/SLSA-flavored predicate, composing the same chain discipline js/provenance/trust-ledger.js already shipped: append() is the only mutator, there is no update or delete, and verifyReceiptChain() re-derives every hash to catch tampering. js/proof-harness/index.js wires all four into runProofCycle() (proposal -> injected engine run -> verdict -> receipt) and confirmProposal() (digest-bound: a statement edit after confirm was requested invalidates it, requiring a fresh Prove), and publishes window.DataGlowProofHarness. canvas/index.html (AUTHORITATIVE) mounts a compact VERDICT panel behind this flag: a claim bar, an editable proposal statement field, a Prove button that resolves the SAME live DuckDB engine Drill Floor's SQL Run/Check path uses (resolveDrillSqlRunQuery / window.engine.runQuery / the DuckDB singleton -- no second wasm load path), a GREEN/RED/GRAY verdict chip with a one-line reason, an expandable receipt (rowCount, duration, digest, statement), and a digest-bound Confirm button. When present, DataGlowTrustLedger.record() also receives a row for each prove cycle. No chat panel; no em dash in any visible text.

proofHarnessV1.description: Proof Harness v1 (VERDICT Harness), building on proofHarness v0 without replacing it. Adds four pillars, composing v0 pure modules rather than duplicating them. (1) Second Engine Rule: js/proof-harness/second-engine.js resolves an optional second engine (an injected runSecondEngine, or window.runDrillPython/pyodide, or window.runDrillR/webr if present) and corroborateRun() compares its result to the primary engine run; runProofCycle() passes this into decideVerdict(), which now gates every candidate GREEN through a corroboration check and pulls it down to RED with reasonCode corroboration-disagree if the two engines do not agree, never silently trusting a single engine when a second one is available and disagrees. No second engine available or injected means v0 single-engine behavior is unchanged. (2) Regression Vault: js/proof-harness/vault.js keeps a durable local (localStorage-backed, never uploaded) set of vault tests; runProofCycle() and rejectProposal() both auto-append a vault test for every RED verdict and every human rejection; runVault()/runVaultCheck() re-run stored tests and report caught versus escaped, so a regression that was once refuted stays caught. (3) Proof Cartridge: js/proof-harness/cartridge.js exports a confirmed GREEN result as a portable JSON cartridge carrying the proposal digest, statement, expected values, verdict, and environment, but zero rows of source data by default, so a proof travels without the data moving; importCartridge() re-executes the statement on the importer's own engine and refuses GREEN with a precise divergence report on any mismatch or broken integrity hash. (4) Proof Inbox: js/proof-harness/inbox.js is a pure review-queue state machine (pending-prove, awaiting-confirm, red, gray, amber, confirmed, rejected) that canvas/index.html renders as the VERDICT panel's default tab, with Prove/Confirm/Reject/Open each reachable in at most two interactions; the panel also gains Vault and Cartridge tabs alongside the v0 Prove tab. js/proof-harness/verdict.js additionally accepts a staleness input and returns a fourth state, AMBER, with reasonCode stale-digest, when a proposal no longer matches the digest an earlier receipt was bound to, never conflating a stale proof with an actively wrong one. No em dash in any visible text.
proofHarnessV1.flagOffBehavior: With proofHarnessV1 off, the Inbox, Vault, and Cartridge tabs and their controls are never mounted or rendered in canvas/index.html, and the panel falls back to the v0 single Prove surface; the pure v1 JS modules (second-engine.js, vault.js, cartridge.js, inbox.js) may still be evaluated and exported on window.DataGlowProofHarness since they make no DOM change themselves, but runProofCycle() only reaches AMBER or corroboration gating when a caller explicitly supplies staleness/priorReceiptDigest or a second engine, so no v0 caller sees any behavior change with the flag off. proofHarness (v0) is unaffected either way; turning proofHarnessV1 off never disables the v0 Prove/Confirm path.

proofHarnessV2.description: Proof Harness v2.0 foundation (PROOF_HARNESS_V2_SPEC.md), building on proofHarness/proofHarnessV1 without replacing them. Adds three pillars. (1) Adversary Pack: js/proof-harness/adversary.js builds at least five metamorphic SQL rewrites (whitespace/case normalize, redundant tautology predicates, an outer SELECT * wrapper, a reordered/second tautology column path, an ORDER BY injection, a double-negated predicate) plus up to two cheap boundary probes (an empty-table WHERE 1=0 equivalent, a COUNT(*) vs COUNT(1) null-safe variant) for any simple SELECT ... FROM ... [WHERE ...] [GROUP BY ...] statement, runs each through the same injected engine, and compares every result back to the primary run with second-engine.js's own epsilon/BigInt-safe comparison discipline. runProofCycle() runs this pack AFTER any second-engine corroboration and wires its report into decideVerdict() as a new gate that mirrors the Second Engine Rule: any failed attack pulls a candidate GREEN down to RED with reasonCode adversary-fail, while zero failures across five or more attacks marks the report strengthensGreen:true; a statement shape the pack cannot safely rewrite is honestly skipped (skipped:true, a reason, never an invented pass) and never blocks GREEN. (2) Excel Claim Path: js/proof-harness/excel-claim.js recognizes one narrow shape, an Excel-style aggregate formula such as SUM(amount), COUNT(claim_id), or AVERAGE(claim_amount)/AVG(claim_amount) with an optional 'on <table>'/'from <table>' clause, and maps it to a quoted DuckDB SELECT statement that runs through the exact same prove cycle as any hand-written SQL claim; cell ranges, multi-sheet 3D references, and VBA/macro content are rejected with a specific reason rather than guessed at. (3) Proof Mesh Attestation: js/proof-harness/mesh-attestation.js exports/imports/compares a dataglow/proof-mesh-attestation/v1 JSON document carrying only digests, a schema fingerprint, the statement text, and the verdict state -- zero rows, ever, enforced by a recursive forbidden-key scan on both export and import -- so two people (or two devices) can agree or diverge on whether they proved the SAME claim without any source data crossing the wire; compareMeshAttestations() reports agreement only when both the claim definition (digest or statement+expected) and the verdict state match, listing every divergent field by name otherwise. canvas/index.html (AUTHORITATIVE) adds an Excel-style claim fill control plus an adversary pass/fail note to the Prove tab, and a mesh attestation export/compare action alongside the existing Cartridge tab, all behind this flag.
proofHarnessV2.flagOffBehavior: With proofHarnessV2 off, the Excel-style claim fill control, the adversary pass/fail note on the Prove tab, and the mesh attestation export/compare action are never mounted or rendered in canvas/index.html. The pure v2 JS modules (adversary.js, excel-claim.js, mesh-attestation.js) may still be evaluated and exported on window.DataGlowProofHarness since they make no DOM change themselves, but runProofCycle() only invokes the adversary pack for a candidate-passing run when a live runQuery was actually supplied, exactly as it already did for the Second Engine Rule; a caller that never exercises these v2 entry points sees byte-for-byte v0/v1 behavior. proofHarness (v0) and proofHarnessV1 are unaffected either way; turning proofHarnessV2 off never disables the v0 Prove/Confirm path or the v1 Inbox/Vault/Cartridge tabs.

questionScout.description: Question Scout (A49_QUESTION_SCOUT_SPEC.md): a local Question Scout panel that proposes candidate analysis questions from the currently loaded table profile (schema + sample stats only, never raw rows to any model). js/question-scout/question-scout.js is the pure engine: buildProfileStrip() (deterministic, no LLM), scoreCandidate()/rankCandidates() (the SPEC's four-hit deterministic keeper filter -- business actor/ops language, real column/table reference, checkable metric type count/rate/share/delta/sum/avg, SELECT-only SQL -- with penalties for viz vanity and columns not in the profile), templateCandidatesFromProfile() (the five-template model-free fallback: grain check, null rate per high-null column, top-N frequency on the top categorical column, min/max/avg on the first numeric column, distinct count on an id-like column, every one labeled 'template (no model)'), buildScoutPrompt()/parseModelCandidates() (prompt construction and tolerant JSON parsing for the on-device model path, pure string logic only), buildProvePrefill() (maps a kept candidate to the Proof Harness's claimText/statement fields, never executes anything), buildBrowseGrounding()/annotateUnverifiedNumbers() (profile-only grounding for Browse mode, flags any numeric assertion 'unverified - run Prove'), and addKeeper()/removeKeeper() (max-5 keepers tray). js/question-scout/data-glow-question-scout-canvas.js is the canvas UI: a slide-in panel with the honest cheating-boundary banner, the profile strip, a Propose button that tries the ALREADY-INLINED local AI bridge (window.OnDeviceLLM from js/narrative/ondevice-llm.js, reusing its loadModel()/isModelLoaded() -- no second model path, no forced download) and falls back to deterministic templates immediately when the model is cold/absent/unavailable, a ranked candidate list with Keep/Edit/Reject, the keepers tray, a Send to Prove action per keeper that prefills the Proof Harness's #dg-ph-claim/#dg-ph-statement fields (or dispatches a dataglow:proof-harness-prefill CustomEvent as a fallback) without ever running SQL itself, and a profile-grounded Browse mode chat. A49.2 (v2, same flag, additive) adds to the same two files: buildJoinHints()/joinCandidatesFromHints() (multi-table join-key hints by name similarity), idrPackCandidates() (a healthcare-idr domain pack that only emits when columns fuzzy-match IDR shape), parseDictionary()/buildScoutPrompt(strip,{dictionary}) (optional column-dictionary grounding), tagAnswerForBrowse() (structured UNVERIFIED badge in Browse mode), keeperPassesFullFilter()/keeperQualityMeter() (how many current keepers pass the full filter), and buildKeepersExport()/exportKeepersJson() (client-side JSON export of the keepers tray). All v2 behavior is opt-in or self-silencing, so a v1-shaped table/profile with no dictionary pasted behaves exactly as before.
questionScout.flagOffBehavior: With questionScout off, the Question Scout button/panel are never mounted in canvas/index.html. No other engine, flag, or panel is touched by this flag; Proof Harness, Trust Ledger, and every other surface behave byte-for-byte as before this PR.
